claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 12 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 12 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I'll guide you through the eligibility assessment. To start, I need some information about the child or children you're applying for.

**What is the age of the child you're inquiring about?**

Please tell me:
- How old is the child (or children)?

The eligibility rules differ depending on whether the child is:
- **Under 16 years old**
- **16 to 19 years old**
- **20 years old or over**

Also, how many children are you applying for in total?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm asking about my child, Alex, who is 12 years old. It's just the one child I'm inquiring about.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 12 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, let me move forward with the next part of the eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is under 16, we've moved to the next check.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not in paid work at all?**

This is just a standard check we need to do for the eligibility process. For children under 16, we want to confirm they're not in full-time employment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. He's just at school like a normal 12-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is not in paid work, so that's a clear "yes" to that check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check one more thing about Alex:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit (UC)?**

In other words, does Alex have their own benefit claim with the DWP (Department for Work and Pensions)? For most 12-year-olds at school, the answer would be "yes" (meaning they're not receiving these benefits), but I want to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular kid at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships. This is a complex criteria node with regional variations:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is 12 and at school, I'd expect the answer is no, but I want to confirm. If Alex were in an apprenticeship, the rules would depend on which part of the UK you're in:
- **England**: Most apprenticeships would disqualify
- **Scotland**: Modern Apprenticeships would disqualify
- **Wales**: Foundation Apprenticeships are approved, but other types would disqualify

But for a 12-year-old in school, this shouldn't apply. Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's only 12 and just goes to regular school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship, so that's straightforward.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now we need to check residency requirements. This is an important part of Child Benefit eligibility.

**Where do you normally live? Specifically:**

Do you (the claimant) normally live in the UK? Or do you have any of the following circumstances:

- **Settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
- **Pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme (with specific conditions like working, studying, or having sufficient resources)
- **Working abroad** as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

For most UK residents, this will be straightforward - you simply normally live in the UK. But I need to confirm your residency situation to proceed.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK, so that meets the residency requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?** This means one of the following:

1. **You live with Alex** - You share a home with him
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - You pay for things like food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, etc., and contribute at least the amount equivalent to Child Benefit
3. **You pay maintenance** - You make payments towards Alex's maintenance under a court order or agreement that covers his upkeep

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex lives with you at home, so you're clearly responsible for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check one more important thing:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

In other words:
- Is Alex's other parent (or anyone else) currently claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Or have you and the other parent agreed who should be the claimant?

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child at a time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So you're the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check where Alex is currently living or staying:

**Is Alex:**
- In hospital?
- In care (residential care home)?
- Fostered?
- Or living at home normally?

Given that you mentioned he's at school and at home with you, I'd expect he's in normal living circumstances, but I want to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living at home normally with me. Nothing unusual – just a regular situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living at home normally with you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're almost there. Just one final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, you're fully responsible for Alex's care and housing costs - the council isn't contributing to his upkeep? For most families in normal circumstances, the answer would be "yes," but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right – the council isn't paying anything towards Alex. I take care of all his needs myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the final confirmation we need. You've met all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! Based on the eligibility assessment, **you are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **Alex meets all the requirements:**
- Alex is 12 years old (under 16)
- Alex is not working full-time
- Alex is not receiving any benefits in his own name
- Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- You are responsible for Alex (he lives with you)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex is living at home normally
- The council is not paying towards Alex's care

**Next Steps to Claim:**

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Gather required documents:**
   - Proof of your identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate
   - Proof of your address if needed

3. **Important to note:** If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the **High Income Child Benefit Charge**, which means you'll need to pay back some or all of the benefit through your tax return.

4. **Payment schedule:** You'll normally receive payments every 4 weeks on a Monday.

For more information and to apply, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Now let me record your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Your eligibility has been recorded. You're all set to move forward with your Child Benefit application for Alex. If you have any other questions or need further assistance, feel free to ask!

reasonings: Alex is eligible for Child Benefit because: (1) Alex is 12 years old, which is under 16 and therefore a qualifying age; (2) Alex is not working full-time (not in paid work); (3) Alex is not receiving Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in his own right; (4) Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship; (5) The claimant normally lives in the UK (Manchester), meeting residency requirements; (6) The claimant is responsible for Alex as he lives at home with the claimant; (7) No other person is claiming Child Benefit for Alex; (8) Alex is living at home in normal circumstances; and (9) The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria are satisfied.
arguments.overall_reasoning: The claimant is eligible to receive Child Benefit for their child Alex. Alex is a qualifying child (under 16, not in disqualifying circumstances), the claimant has responsibility for Alex (living together), the claimant meets residency requirements (living in the UK), and no council support is being received. The family meets all legal requirements for Child Benefit eligibility. The claimant should now proceed to apply through the official channels, and be aware of potential High Income Child Benefit Charge implications if household income exceeds £60,000."
